name: Now You Don't
flavor: The curtain drops for exactly one second. When it rises, you're not where the audience is looking anymore.
description: You vanish behind a snap of silk and misdirection, becoming invisible until the start of your next turn or until you make an attack roll, force a saving throw, or force an ability check, whichever comes first. As part of casting this, you may also move up to 10 feet without provoking opportunity attacks — the last thing anyone saw of you was already the wrong direction. This is misdirection, not true invisibility, and it can be beaten by simply watching you properly: each creature that can see you at the moment you cast it makes a Wisdom (Perception) check against your {{trick save DC|8 + proficiency bonus + your trick ability modifier}}. **If any one of them succeeds, the trick ends immediately for everybody** — they call out where you went, the room's eyes follow, and you are simply standing there. One person seeing through it is enough; there is never a state where you are hidden from some creatures and not others.
narration: The curtain drops for exactly one second. When it lifts you are not where anyone is looking — until somebody who was watching your feet instead of your hands points and shouts, and then the whole room is looking at you again.
sheetSummary: Invisible until the start of your next turn or until you attack or force a save or check; may move 10 ft without provoking as part of the trick. Each creature that can SEE you cast it makes a Wisdom (Perception) check vs {{trick save DC|8 + proficiency bonus + your trick ability modifier}} — ANY success ends it for everyone. Never partial: you are hidden from all of them or none.
